mainTopic: Rejected offerings (דחוי), רב חסדא's rule on when bird pairs get their roles, rich and poor offerings, and the משנה on the order of names in the תורה
overview: The amud opens at the end of a ruling: birds that a wealthy man set aside in place of his lamb stay rejected even after he becomes poor. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע learns three rules from this, and רבי שמעון's view about the offspring of a female set aside for a פסח seems to challenge them. The answer is that the rules follow the רבנן, while רבי שמעון holds that live animals are not rejected and that the יום כיפור lottery is not essential. Next, רב חסדא rules that a bird pair gets its roles only when the owner buys it or when the כהן offers it. Two ברייתות are brought against him, one about the יום כיפור goats and one about a poor מטמא מקדש who became rich, and both are reread so that they fit his rule. This leads to a debate about whether a rich person fulfills his duty with a poor person's קרבן. The גמרא concludes that only a rich מצורע fails, because of the words זאת and הוא in the פסוקים. A new משנה then teaches that the order of names in the תורה does not rank lambs and goats, two kinds of birds, or father and mother. In practice, though, the father comes before the mother and a son's main רב comes before the father. The גמרא begins a ברייתא about four cries of the Temple courtyard, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Since it was rejected, it stays rejected
steps.stepSummary: This is the end of a ruling. A wealthy man set aside birds in place of his female lamb and then became poor. The birds stay rejected for good.
steps.simpleTranslation: [If he set aside birds in place of] his female lamb and then became poor, since the birds were rejected, they stay rejected.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ruling that started just before this section. A man set aside birds when he was rich, and they do not become usable later, even after he becomes poor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While he was rich he owed a female lamb, so birds were never a valid offering for him. Once he becomes poor, birds would normally be exactly what he should bring. Still, the rule of הואיל ונדחה ידחה says that once these specific birds were pushed off, they can never come back.

keyTerms.meaning: Since it was rejected, it stays rejected for good
A female lamb, the offering a wealthy person brings
He became poor

phrases.english: [in place of] his female lamb, and he became poor.
phrases.notes: The sentence starts on the previous page: a wealthy man set aside birds in place of the lamb he owed.

phrases.english: Since it was rejected, it stays rejected.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a ruling that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Birds set aside by a wealthy man in place of a lamb stay rejected even after he becomes poor.

steps.title: Three rules learned from the birds case
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע learns three rules from this ruling. Live animals can be rejected, קדושת דמים can be rejected, and something rejected from the start counts as rejected.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע said: Learn three things from this. Live animals can be rejected. Holiness of value can be rejected. And something rejected from the very beginning counts as rejected.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע takes the birds ruling and pulls three general rules out of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, the birds are alive and have no blemish, yet they are permanently rejected. So live animals can be rejected. Second, when he was rich the birds could not be offered for him, so they held only קדושת דמים, and still they were rejected. Third, the birds were never fit even for a moment, so even a rejection from the very start counts as a real rejection.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this; we can conclude from it
Live animals can be permanently rejected
Holiness that rests only on an item's money value, not on the item itself as an offering
Rejected from the very beginning, never fit at all

steps.whatToRemember: Three rules come from the birds case: live animals can be rejected, קדושת דמים can be rejected, and something rejected from the start counts as rejected.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up 'rejected from the start' with 'fit and later rejected.' The third rule says even something that was never fit at all is still truly rejected.
steps.whyThisMatters: These three rules are the target of the objection in the next step. They also matter for many other cases of rejected offerings.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ,
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
Learn three things from this:
Learn from it that live animals can be rejected.
And holiness of value (is rejected).
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets, but the meaning stays the same: קדושת דמים can be rejected.

phrases.english: And something rejected from the beginning counts as rejected.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws general rules out of the ruling in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Live animals can be rejected, קדושת דמים can be rejected, and something rejected from the start counts as rejected.

steps.title: Challenge from a female set aside for a קרבן פסח
steps.stepSummary: רב עוקבא בר חמא quotes a ברייתא. A female set aside for a קרבן פסח, and the male she later gives birth to, are both left to graze until blemished, then sold to buy a קרבן פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עוקבא בר חמא objected: Someone sets aside a female for his קרבן פסח before פסח. She grazes until she gets a blemish, then she is sold and he brings a קרבן פסח with the money. If she gave birth to a male, he grazes until he gets a blemish, then he is sold and a קרבן פסח is brought with his money.
steps.whatsHappening: רב עוקבא בר חמא begins to attack רב הונא's three rules by quoting a ברייתא. This step lays out the source, and the point of the attack comes right after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קרבן פסח must be a male, so a female set aside for it can never be offered. She holds only קדושת דמים: she waits for a blemish, and her money buys the offering. This first opinion treats her male offspring the same way, which fits רב הונא's rules. The objection will come from רבי שמעון's dissent in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A female animal set aside for a קרבן פסח, which must be male
She grazes until she gets a blemish (and may then be redeemed)
With her money, from selling her
She gave birth to a male

phrases.english: Rav Ukva bar Chama objected:
One who sets aside a female for his Paschal offering before Passover,
she grazes until she becomes blemished,
phrases.notes: A קרבן פסח must be male, so she can't be offered. They wait for a blemish so she can be sold.

phrases.english: and she is sold, and he brings a Paschal offering with her money.
If she gave birth to a male,
he grazes until he becomes blemished,
and he is sold, and he brings a Paschal offering with his money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes a ברייתא to challenge the three rules of step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's three rules about rejection.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first part of the ברייתא sets up the case. In step 4, רבי שמעון's view that the offspring itself is offered will be used against the rule בעלי חיים נדחים.

steps.title: רבי שמעון says the offspring itself is offered
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: רבי שמעון says the male offspring itself is brought as a פסח. The גמרא concludes that live animals are not rejected, which challenges רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: the male offspring itself is offered as a פסח. Learn from this that live animals are not rejected!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the ברייתא it started quoting in step 3. It uses רבי שמעון's opinion to attack the rule from step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mother was set aside for a פסח, but a female can never be a פסח. Even so, רבי שמעון lets her offspring, which carries her holiness, be offered. So a live animal's holiness was not pushed away for good, which goes against the rule that בעלי חיים נדחים.

keyTerms.meaning: It itself, meaning the male offspring, not money from selling it
Learn from this; the גמרא draws a conclusion
Live animals
Are rejected, pushed off permanently from being offered

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
It itself is offered as a Pesach.
phrases.notes: "It" is the male born to the female that was set aside for a פסח (step 3).

phrases.english: Learn from this,
live animals are not rejected!

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ, בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים אֵינָם נִדְחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in step 3 and states the challenge it creates.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's first rule from step 2: בעלי חיים נדחים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The mother could never be a פסח, yet her offspring is offered as one. That shows live animals are not permanently rejected.

steps.title: The rule follows the Rabbis; רבי שמעון disagrees
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי אושעיא answer that the rule 'live animals are rejected' follows the רבנן. רבי שמעון really holds they are not rejected, and he also holds the lottery is not essential.
steps.simpleTranslation: דבי רבי אושעיא say: When we said live animals are rejected, that was according to the רבנן. רבי שמעון does hold that live animals are not rejected, and that the lottery is not essential.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It admits רבי שמעון disagrees and says the rule from step 2 follows the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is pushed aside here. The two views are simply split. The רבנן (the תנא קמא of step 3) say the offspring is sold, so live animals can be rejected. רבי שמעון holds the opposite, and he also holds a second rule: the lottery for the יום כיפור goats is not essential.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis, the majority opinion (here, the first opinion in the ברייתא)
He holds, this is his opinion
The lottery that decides which יום כיפור goat is for ה' and which is sent away

steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not say רבי שמעון agrees with the rule. It says the rule follows the רבנן, and רבי שמעון truly holds that live animals are not rejected.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Oshaya say:
When we said it, it was according to the Rabbis;
Rabbi Shimon holds
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the letter ד in the round brackets, so this reads as a new sentence about רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: that live animals are not rejected,
and that the lottery is not essential.
phrases.notes: This is the lottery for the two goats of יום כיפור.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי דְּבֵי רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא: כִּי אָמְרִינַן לְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the opinions: the rule follows the רבנן, and רבי שמעון disagrees.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule בעלי חיים נדחים was assumed to be accepted by everyone, so רבי שמעון seemed to contradict it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule follows the רבנן. רבי שמעון consistently holds that live animals are not rejected and that the lottery is not essential.

steps.title: Proof from the Yom Kippur goats
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that if one of the יום כיפור goats dies, רבי שמעון says a replacement is brought without a lottery.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: If one of the goats died, he brings a partner for the other one without a lottery. These are the words of רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to prove the two views it just credited to רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום כיפור two goats are chosen by lottery, one for ה' and one to be sent away. If one dies, רבי שמעון keeps the surviving goat in its role and pairs it with a new goat, and he does not draw a new lottery.

keyTerms.meaning: One of them died (one of the two יום כיפור goats)
Its partner, a new goat to pair with the surviving one
Without a lottery

phrases.english: As it is taught:
If one of them died,
phrases.notes: "Them" means the two goats of יום כיפור after the lottery was drawn.

phrases.english: he brings a partner for it without a lottery,
these are the words of Rabbi Shimon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source for the views credited to רבי שמעון in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון holds live animals are not rejected and that the lottery is not essential.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about one of the יום כיפור goats dying.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's two views are confirmed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes from the ברייתא that רבי שמעון holds live animals are not rejected and the lottery is not essential.
steps.simpleTranslation: Evidently he holds that live animals are not rejected, and that the lottery is not essential.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out what the goat ברייתא proves and closes the answer to the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When its partner died, the surviving goat could not be used, yet it becomes fit again once a new partner is brought. So live animals are not permanently rejected. The new goat is brought with no lottery, so the lottery is not essential.

keyTerms.meaning: Evidently, so we see
He holds
Essential; without it the מצוה does not work

steps.whatToRemember: The rule בעלי חיים נדחים follows the רבנן. רבי שמעון disagrees: for him live animals are not rejected for good, and the יום כיפור lottery is not essential.

phrases.english: Evidently he holds
that live animals are not rejected,
and that the lottery is not essential.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא קָסָבַר בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים אֵינָן נִידְחִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the ברייתא in step 6.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי שמעון consistently holds that live animals are not rejected and that the lottery is not essential. The rule from step 2 stands according to the רבנן.

steps.title: רב חסדא: when a pair of birds gets assigned
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that קינין are assigned as עולה or חטאת only when the owner buys them or when the כהן offers them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא says: A pair of birds is only assigned (which one is the עולה and which is the חטאת) either when the owner buys them, or when the כהן offers them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ruling from רב חסדא about when bird pairs get their specific roles.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קן is two birds, one to be a חטאת and one an עולה. רב חסדא says there are only two moments when the roles can be fixed: when the owner buys them or when the כהן does the offering. At any other time, a designation does not take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: Nests: pairs of birds brought as offerings, one עולה and one חטאת
Are designated, meaning each bird is given its specific role
The owner's purchase of the birds
The כהן's act of offering the bird

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling is the basis that the rest of the section will challenge and defend.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda says:
Nests are not designated,
phrases.notes: "Nests" means pairs of birds. "Designated" means deciding which bird is the עולה and which is the חטאת.

phrases.english: except either at the owner's purchase,
or at the priest's offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: אֵין הַקִּינִּין מִתְפָּרְשׁוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section about bird offerings, separate from the earlier discussion of rejected animals.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bird pairs are assigned only at the owner's purchase or at the כהן's offering.

steps.title: The source for רב חסדא's rule
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר אשי explains that רב חסדא learns his rule from two פסוקים: one about the owner taking the birds, and one about the כהן doing the offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר אשי said: What is רב חסדא's reason? Because it is written, "And she shall take two turtledoves..." and "And the כהן shall do...". This means the assigning happens either when the owner buys them or when the כהן offers them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי בר אשי asks for רב חסדא's source and answers it himself with two פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One פסוק connects the roles of the birds to the owner's taking. The other connects them to the כהן's doing. Together they show the two moments when the roles can be fixed, which is exactly רב חסדא's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason or source?
"And she shall take": the owner's purchase
"And the כהן shall do": the כהן's offering

phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Ashi said:
What is the reason of Rav Chisda?
As it is written: "And she shall take two turtledoves, etc."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 12:8

phrases.english: and "And the priest shall do, etc."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:30

phrases.english: either at the owner's purchase,
or at the priest's offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the scriptural source for רב חסדא's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's rule that birds are assigned only at purchase or at offering.

steps.title: Challenge: only the lottery makes the goat a sin offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא with a ברייתא about the יום כיפור goats. It says only the גורל makes the goat a חטאת. Saying its name does not, and the כהן's act does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: "And he shall make it a חטאת" teaches that the lottery makes it a חטאת. Saying its name does not make it a חטאת, and the כהן does not make it a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins quoting a ברייתא about the יום כיפור goats in order to challenge רב חסדא. This step sets up the challenge, and step 13 explains it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This step only quotes the start of the ברייתא about the יום כיפור goats: only the lottery makes the goat a חטאת. The problem for רב חסדא is not stated yet. Step 13 spells it out: the ברייתא compares naming to the lottery, and the lottery is done neither at buying nor at offering.

keyTerms.meaning: "And he shall make it a חטאת" (ויקרא 16:9)
The lottery used to pick the two יום כיפור goats
The name, meaning saying out loud "this is a חטאת"

steps.confusionAlert: This ברייתא is about goats on יום כיפור, not birds. The challenge does not come from the words 'the כהן does not make it a חטאת'. It comes from the ברייתא comparing naming to the lottery (step 13).

phrases.english: They raised an objection: "And he shall make it a sin offering"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 16:9, about the יום כיפור goat chosen by lottery.

phrases.english: the lottery makes it a sin offering,
but the name does not make it a sin offering,
phrases.notes: Saying out loud "this one is a חטאת" is not enough.

phrases.english: and the priest does not make it a sin offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule set up in steps 8-9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's rule that naming assigns bird pairs only at the owner's buying or the כהן's offering.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא goes on to compare naming with the lottery, and the lottery is not tied to buying or offering. So naming would not be tied to those times either (step 13).

steps.title: The ברייתא's קל וחומר that the verse comes to block
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains why a פסוק was needed. Without it, one might argue by קל וחומר: a bird pair cannot be assigned by lottery but can be assigned by name, so the goats, which can be assigned by lottery, should surely be assigned by name too.
steps.simpleTranslation: A פסוק is needed, because you might have thought: Isn't it logical? If in a case where a lottery does not assign, saying the name does assign, then in a case where a lottery does assign, shouldn't saying the name also assign?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and explains why the פסוק was needed. It shows the logical argument the פסוק comes to block.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With bird pairs, a lottery cannot fix the roles, yet saying the name does. So you might think the name is even stronger where a lottery does work, as with the יום כיפור goats. The פסוק "ועשהו חטאת" teaches that this קל וחומר is wrong: for the goats, only the lottery counts.

keyTerms.meaning: Because one might have thought
Isn't it logical? The opening of a קל וחומר
Sanctified, here meaning gave the animal its specific role
Reasoning from a weaker case to a stronger case

phrases.english: For one might have said: Is it not logical,
if in a place where the lottery does not sanctify,
phrases.notes: Like a bird pair: you can't use a lottery to decide which bird is which.

phrases.english: the name does sanctify,
then in a place where the lottery does sanctify,
phrases.notes: The יום כיפור goats.

phrases.english: is it not logical that the name should sanctify?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא used for the challenge, explaining why its פסוק was needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: Same target as step 10: רב חסדא's view.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's reasoning builds the case that leads to the פסוק excluding name and כהן. This continues to set up the contradiction with רב חסדא.

steps.title: The ברייתא ends with the פסוק: only the lottery makes the goat a חטאת
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its argument. The פסוק 'וְעָשָׂהוּ חַטָּאת' teaches that the גורל makes the goat a חטאת, and saying its name does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore the פסוק says 'And he shall make it a sin offering.' The lottery makes it a חטאת; saying the name does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from the last step finishes. It quotes a פסוק that blocks the קל וחומר it just built.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 11 the ברייתא argued that naming should work for the goats, since it works for bird pairs. The פסוק overrides that logic: for the goats, only the גורל counts. This sets up the גמרא's challenge to רב חסדא in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And he shall make it a sin offering' (ויקרא 16:9)
Lottery used to pick which goat is for ה׳ and which is for עזאזל
Saying out loud what the animal is for (its 'name')

phrases.english: Therefore the verse says: "And he shall make it a sin offering,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 16:9

phrases.english: the lottery makes it a sin offering,
but the name does not make it a sin offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא's קל וחומר from step 11 by citing the פסוק that cancels it.
steps.raayaObject: That for the יום כיפור goats, only the גורל assigns the goat as a חטאת

steps.title: The ברייתא treats naming like the lottery, which is not tied to buying or offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the challenge. The ברייתא compares naming to the lottery. The lottery happens neither at buying nor at offering, so naming should not need to happen then either. That goes against רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא puts the name side by side with the lottery. Just as the lottery is not done at buying or at offering, naming would also not be done at buying or at offering!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains exactly why the ברייתא is a problem for רב חסדא. It is reading the קל וחומר as comparing naming to the lottery in every way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא said naming only works at the owner's buying or the כהן's offering. In the ברייתא's argument, naming is placed right next to the lottery. The lottery is done at neither of those times, so naming would seem to work at any time. That contradicts רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: Similar to, parallel to
Taking or buying the animals (by the owner)
Doing or offering the sacrifice (by the כהן)

phrases.english: It teaches the name as similar to the lottery:
just as the lottery is not at the buying
and not at the offering,
so too the name as well
is not at the buying and not at the offering!
phrases.notes: In other words, naming would work at any time. That clashes with רב חסדא from step 8.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out the implication of the ברייתא (steps 10-12) that clashes with רב חסדא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's rule that קינין are assigned only at the owner's buying or the כהן's offering
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא pairs naming with the lottery. The lottery is not tied to buying or offering, so naming should not be either.

steps.title: רב rereads the ברייתא's קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: רב explains the ברייתא differently. For bird pairs, the lottery cannot assign them at buying or offering, but naming can at either time. For the goats, the lottery works even outside those times. So surely naming should work at buying or offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: this is what the ברייתא means. For bird pairs, the lottery does not assign them at the owner's buying or the כהן's offering, yet naming does assign them at either of those times. Here, with the goats, the lottery assigns them even though it is not done at buying or offering. Isn't it logical that naming should assign them at buying or offering?
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the challenge by explaining what the ברייתא's argument really meant. In his reading, naming is still tied to buying or offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed the ברייתא made naming exactly like the lottery. רב says the comparison is only about strength: the goats can be assigned more easily than the birds. Even so, the naming in the argument still happens 'either at buying or at offering', just as רב חסדא said.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (rereading a text)
Isn't it logical? The opening of a קל וחומר conclusion
Set it apart for a specific offering
The owners who bring the offering

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רב is saying naming works for the goats. He is only explaining the logic the ברייתא considered and then rejects with the פסוק. The point is that even this rejected logic assumes naming happens at buying or offering.

phrases.english: Rav said, this is what it is saying:
And if in a place where the lottery did not sanctify
at the owner's buying and at the priest's offering,
the name did sanctify,

phrases.aramaic: אִי בִּלְקִיחַת בְּעָלִים אִי בַּעֲשִׂיַּית כֹּהֵן.
phrases.english: either at the owner's buying or at the priest's offering.
here, where the lottery does sanctify
not at the buying and not at the offering,
is it not logical that the name should sanctify,
either at the buying or at the offering?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13 by rereading the ברייתא's קל וחומר.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא compared naming to the lottery in every way, including timing, so naming would work at any time.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא only compares how strong each method is. Naming is still tied to buying or offering, which fits רב חסדא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This saves רב חסדא's rule. It shows that even the ברייתא's rejected logic assumes naming happens at buying or offering.

steps.title: Under רב's reading, the פסוק still says only the lottery counts
steps.stepSummary: With רב's reading in place, the ברייתא's ending is repeated. The פסוק teaches that for the goats only the גורל works. Naming does not work, even at buying or offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore the פסוק says 'And he shall make it a sin offering.' The lottery makes it a חטאת; saying the name does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the end of the ברייתא to finish רב's reading of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words are the same as in step 12, but now they reject naming 'at buying or at offering'. That fits רב חסדא's rule, so the challenge is answered.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore the פסוק says, which brings a verse to settle the question

steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא: naming assigns קינין only at the owner's buying or the כהן's offering. The ברייתא about the goats fits this, as רב reads it. For the goats, the פסוק says only the גורל counts.

phrases.english: Therefore the verse says: "And he shall make it a sin offering,"
the lottery makes it a sin offering,
but the name does not make it a sin offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב's rereading by restating the ברייתא's verse with its new meaning.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא does not contradict רב חסדא. Naming only matters at buying or offering, and for the goats the פסוק says only the גורל counts.

steps.title: A ברייתא about a poor man who became rich
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. A poor person who must bring birds for entering the מקדש while טמא set aside money for them, then became rich. He labeled one part of the money for his חטאת and one part for his עולה. He may use the חטאת money toward his new obligation, but not the עולה money.
steps.simpleTranslation: They objected: A poor person who entered the מקדש while impure set aside money for his pair of birds, and then he became rich. If he said 'This money is for my חטאת and this money is for my עולה,' he adds more money and brings what he now owes from the חטאת money. He may not add money and bring it from the עולה money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new challenge against רב חסדא by quoting a ברייתא. In the next step it will explain why this ברייתא is a problem for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A poor person who is מטמא מקדש brings two birds, one as a חטאת and one as an עולה. A rich person brings a female sheep or goat as a חטאת. The ברייתא says the labels he gave the money stick: the חטאת money can go toward the new חטאת, but the עולה money cannot.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who entered the מקדש (or ate holy food) while טמא
A pair of birds (his pair of birds), one for a חטאת and one for an עולה
He set aside money for a קרבן
He became rich
His obligation, the קרבן he now has to bring

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of money. Only the money labeled for the חטאת can be used for the rich man's new חטאת. The money labeled for the עולה cannot be switched to a חטאת.

phrases.english: They raised an objection: a poor person who made the Temple impure
who set aside money for his pair of birds,
and then became rich.
If he said: 'This money is for my sin offering
and this money is for my burnt offering' –
he adds more money and brings his obligation from the sin-offering money,
phrases.notes: Now that he is rich, he owes a sheep or goat as a חטאת. Birds are no longer enough.

phrases.english: but he does not add money and bring it from the burnt-offering money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first ברייתא was explained in a way that fits רב חסדא, a second ברייתא is brought against him.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's rule that naming a קרבן only counts at the time of buying or offering
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא shows a naming that counts even though it was done when he only set the money aside, not when buying or offering.

steps.title: Why the ברייתא goes against רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the problem. In the ברייתא the money was named neither at buying nor at offering, yet the names count. That contradicts רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here there is neither buying nor offering, and the ברייתא still teaches that he brings his obligation from the חטאת money and not from the עולה money!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains exactly why the ברייתא it just quoted is a challenge to רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא holds that a name only takes hold at the moment of buying the animal or offering it. Here the man only labeled money, and no animal was bought or offered yet. Since the ברייתא treats the labels as binding, naming seems to work at any time.

keyTerms.meaning: Buying, the moment the animal is purchased
Doing, the moment the קרבן is offered

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא הָכָא דְּלֵיכָּא לָא לְקִיחָה וְלָא עֲשִׂיָּיה,
phrases.english: But here, where there is neither buying nor offering,
phrases.notes: He only named the money. No animal was bought or brought yet.

phrases.english: and it teaches: he brings his obligation from the sin-offering money,
and not from the burnt-offering money!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא הָכָא דְּלֵיכָּא לָא לְקִיחָה וְלָא עֲשִׂיָּיה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the ברייתא from step 16 contradicts רב חסדא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Naming the money, which happened outside buying or offering, still fixed what the money could be used for.

steps.title: רב ששת questions the ברייתא's wording
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers that the ברייתא as worded cannot be right. A rich person cannot fulfill his obligation with a poor person's קרבן. So naming money for the birds after he became rich should mean nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: Do you really think this ברייתא is worded correctly when it says 'and he became rich'? But רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי אושעיא: a rich person who made the מקדש impure and brought a poor person's קרבן has not fulfilled his obligation!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת pushes back on the challenge by showing that the ברייתא itself has a problem in how it is worded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי אושעיא, once a person is rich, the poor man's birds are useless for him. If he named the money for those birds after he became rich, his naming should have no effect at all. So the ברייתא cannot mean what it seems to say, and it cannot be used against רב חסדא as it stands.

keyTerms.meaning: And do you really think? This introduces doubt about the proof
A ברייתא that is worded correctly
A poor person's קרבן, here the pair of birds
He has not fulfilled his obligation

steps.whatToRemember: The challenge from the ברייתא rests on the words 'and he became rich.' רב ששת shows those words clash with רבי אושעיא's rule, so the ברייתא's wording is in doubt.
steps.whyThisMatters: Instead of answering for רב חסדא directly, רב ששת weakens the proof by showing the source does not make sense as worded.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: And do you really think
that this baraita is correctly worded,
since it teaches 'and he became rich'?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא:
phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Elazar say in the name of Rabbi Oshaya:
A rich person who made the Temple impure
who brought a poor person's offering has not fulfilled his obligation!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 17 by attacking how the ברייתא is worded.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the ברייתא, as currently worded, as a proof against רב חסדא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא says the man named the money after becoming rich. But a rich person cannot fulfill his obligation with a poor person's קרבן, so his naming should mean nothing.

steps.title: The money was named back when he was still poor
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת finishes his answer. The ברייתא must mean the naming happened while the man was poor, at the moment he set the money aside. So it does not contradict רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what else can you say? You must say he already named the money when he was poor. So too, you can say he already named it at the moment he set it aside.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת completes his defense of רב חסדא. Since naming after becoming rich would mean nothing, the ברייתא must be talking about naming done earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 showed the plain wording of the ברייתא cannot be right, so everyone has to reread it. If we already have to say he named the money while he was poor, we can just as easily say he named it at the time he set it aside. Then the naming fits a time that רב חסדא accepts, and his rule stands.

keyTerms.meaning: His time of being poor
The moment he set aside the money for the offering
So too, in the same way

phrases.english: Rather, what do you have to say?
That he already said it from the time he was poor
phrases.notes: "Said it" means he declared: this money is for my חטאת and this for my עולה.

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי נָמֵי שֶׁכְּבָר אָמַר מִשְּׁעַת הַפְרָשָׁתוֹ.
phrases.english: So too, he already said it from the time he set it aside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב ששת's answer that began in step 18
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the case in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא describes naming money after he became rich, which is neither at buying nor at offering
steps.terutzMaskana: The naming happened while he was poor, at the time he set the money aside, so רב חסדא is not contradicted

steps.title: How would רבי חגא explain the ברייתא?
steps.stepSummary: רבי חגא, quoting רבי אושעיא, says a rich person who brings a poor person's קרבן has fulfilled his duty. By his view, the ברייתא makes sense as written, so the contradiction to רב חסדא seems to come back.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי חגא, who says in the name of רבי אושעיא that he has fulfilled his duty, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. That answer only works for someone who holds that a rich person cannot use a poor person's קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת had to reread the ברייתא only because a rich person supposedly cannot use a poor person's offering. רבי חגא says he can, so for him nothing is wrong with the ברייתא as written. That means the ברייתא again shows naming that counts even though it was neither at buying nor at offering, which goes against רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: He has fulfilled his duty
What can be said? How would he explain it? (the next step answers this)

phrases.english: But according to Rabbi Ḥagga, who says in the name of Rabbi Oshaya,
who says he has fulfilled his duty,
what can be said?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי חַגָּא אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא דְּאָמַר יָצָא, מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that step 19's answer depends on one side of a מחלוקת
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's rule, by way of רב ששת's answer
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For רבי חגא nothing forces a rereading of the ברייתא, so the plain ברייתא contradicts רב חסדא again

steps.title: Read the ברייתא as naming at the time of buying
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the wording of the ברייתא: after he became rich, he bought the animals and named them then. That naming was at buying, which fits רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Teach the ברייתא this way: and afterward he bought the animals and said which was which.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי חגא by reading the ברייתא differently. The naming took place when the animals were bought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא says naming works at buying or at offering. If the ברייתא is read as saying he named them when he bought them, the naming happened at a time that counts. So even by רבי חגא's view, the ברייתא no longer goes against רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: He bought

phrases.english: Teach: and afterward he bought and said.
phrases.notes: He bought the animals after becoming rich and named them at that moment. Buying is one of the times רב חסדא accepts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא describes naming the money with no buying involved
steps.terutzMaskana: The naming happened at the time of buying, so it fits רב חסדא
steps.whatToRemember: By either view, the ברייתא is read so the naming happened at a time רב חסדא accepts: either back when he was poor and set the money aside, or when he bought the animals.

steps.title: A ברייתא about a מצורע seems to refute רבי חגא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a poor מצורע who brought a rich person's קרבן has fulfilled his duty. But a rich מצורע who brought a poor person's קרבן has not. That seems to refute רבי חגא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: a poor מצורע who brought a rich person's קרבן has fulfilled his duty. A rich one who brought a poor person's קרבן has not. This is a refutation of רבי חגא in the name of רבי אושעיא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now attacks רבי חגא's view directly. It brings a ברייתא where a rich person does not fulfill his duty with a poor person's קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חגא says a rich person who brings a poor person's offering has fulfilled his duty. The ברייתא says clearly that a rich מצורע who does this has not. It looks like a clear source against him.

keyTerms.meaning: A person struck with צרעת, who must bring offerings when he becomes pure
The offering of a rich person (animals)
The offering of a poor person (cheaper, usually birds)
A refutation, a strong challenge that seems to knock down a view

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: מְצוֹרָע עָנִי שֶׁהֵבִיא קׇרְבַּן עָשִׁיר – יָצָא,
phrases.english: A poor leper who brought a rich person's offering has fulfilled his duty;

phrases.aramaic: עָשִׁיר שֶׁהֵבִיא קׇרְבַּן עָנִי – לֹא יָצָא,
phrases.english: a rich one who brought a poor person's offering has not fulfilled it.

phrases.aramaic: תְּיוּבְתָּא דְּרַבִּי חַגָּא אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא!
phrases.english: This is a refutation of Rabbi Ḥagga in the name of Rabbi Oshaya!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: מְצוֹרָע עָנִי שֶׁהֵבִיא קׇרְבַּן עָשִׁיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defending רב חסדא to challenging רבי חגא's own view
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חגא's rule that a rich person fulfills his duty with a poor person's קרבן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says outright that a rich מצורע who brought a poor person's קרבן has not fulfilled his duty

steps.title: The מצורע is a special case because of the word ״זֹאת״
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers on רבי חגא's behalf that a מצורע is different. The תורה wrote ״זֹאת״, which limits the מצורע to his proper offering. Outside of a מצורע, a rich person can still fulfill his duty with a poor person's קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: He could say to you: a מצורע is different, because the תורה limited it with the word ״זֹאת״ ('this').
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי חגא. The ברייתא's rule applies only to a מצורע, because of a special word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״זֹאת״ in the פסוק about the מצורע teaches that he must bring exactly the offering that fits him. So the ברייתא is an exception for the מצורע alone. It does not show the general rule for other cases, so רבי חגא's view stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different (a special case)
The תורה excluded or limited
"This", a word in the פסוק that limits the law

steps.confusionAlert: Don't take this to mean a מצורע's offering works differently in every way. The word ״זֹאת״ only blocks a rich מצורע from using a poor person's offering. רבי חגא's general rule still applies elsewhere.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי חגא holds that a rich person can fulfill his duty with a poor person's קרבן. The מצורע is the exception, learned from ״זֹאת״.

phrases.english: He could say to you:
It is different with a leper,
because the Merciful One limited it with "This."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:2

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the refutation of step 22
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to a special case learned from a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא about the מצורע shows a general rule that a rich person never fulfills his duty with a poor person's קרבן
steps.terutzMaskana: The מצורע is an exception because of ״זֹאת״, so רבי חגא's general rule stands

steps.title: Then even a poor מצורע with a rich offering should fail
steps.stepSummary: If ״זאת״ limits the מצורע to his exact offering, then a poor מצורע who brought a rich offering should also not fulfill his duty.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then even a poor מצורע who brought a rich person's offering should not fulfill his duty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 23. If ״זאת״ means the מצורע must bring exactly his own offering, it should block the poor מצורע who brought a rich offering too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״זאת״ sounds like a strict limit: only this offering works. If so, it should cut both ways. But the ברייתא in Step 22 said a poor מצורע who brought the rich offering did fulfill his duty.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if what you said is true
A person with the skin disease צרעת, who brings special offerings when he becomes pure
The rich person's (more expensive) offering

phrases.english: If so,
phrases.notes: If ״זֹאת״ limits the מצורע to the offering that fits him.

phrases.english: then even a poor מצורע too
who brought a rich person's offering should not fulfill his duty!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, אֲפִילּוּ מְצוֹרָע עָנִי נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading of ״זאת″ given in Step 23
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of ״זאת״ as a limit on the מצורע
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A limiting word should limit in both directions, but the ברייתא lets a poor מצורע use a rich offering.

steps.title: The word תורת brings the poor מצורע back in
steps.stepSummary: No. The פסוק adds the word ״תורת״, which includes the poor מצורע who brought a rich offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: Not so. The פסוק came back and wrote ״תורת״.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the תורה added another word, ״תורת״, which brings back the poor מצורע who brought the rich offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״זאת״ alone would have blocked every changed offering. ״תורת״ includes one case, the poor man who brings more than he must. So only the rich man who brings less stays blocked.

keyTerms.meaning: No, that is not so
The פסוק came back (to include it)
"The law of"; a word used here to include a case

phrases.english: Not so,
for the פסוק came back and wrote "the law of".
phrases.notes: The word תורת includes a case that ״זֹאת״ would have left out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 24
steps.terutzResolutionType: A second word in the פסוק includes one case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״זאת״ blocks both the poor and the rich מצורע who changed offerings
steps.terutzMaskana: ״תורת״ includes the poor מצורע, so ״זאת״ blocks only the rich one

steps.title: A ברייתא spells out both words
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא confirms it. ״תורת״ includes the poor מצורע with a rich offering, and ״זאת״ excludes the rich מצורע with a poor offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: ״תורת״ includes a poor מצורע who brought a rich offering, so he fulfilled his duty. One might think even a rich one who brought a poor offering fulfilled his duty. So the פסוק says ״זאת״.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what it just explained. Each word of the פסוק has its own job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא assigns ״תורת״ to include and ״זאת״ to exclude. This shows the answer in Step 25 is not made up but is taught in a ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: To include
One might have thought
Therefore the פסוק says (to teach otherwise)

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:
"The law of" comes to include a poor מצורע
who brought a rich person's offering: he fulfilled his duty.
One might think that even a rich one
who brought a poor person's offering has fulfilled his duty?
Therefore the פסוק says: "This".

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of Step 25 with a ברייתא
steps.raayaObject: That ״תורת״ includes the poor מצורע and ״זאת״ excludes the rich one
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on the מצורע's offerings

steps.title: Learn the rule for all offerings from the מצורע
steps.stepSummary: Why not learn from the מצורע that any rich person who brings a poor offering does not fulfill his duty?
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us learn from it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why we don't apply the מצורע rule to every sliding-scale offering. That would mean a rich person who brings a poor offering never fulfills his duty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תורה blocks a rich מצורע with a poor offering, maybe that is a general rule. If so, רבי חגא's view would fall.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us learn a general rule from it

phrases.english: But let us learn from it!
phrases.notes: Learn from the מצורע to all other offerings that change by wealth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי חגא again, now by spreading the מצורע rule
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חגא's claim that the rule is limited to the מצורע
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rule written for one sliding-scale offering should apply to the others.

steps.title: The word הוא keeps the rule for the מצורע only
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says ״ואם דל הוא״. The word הוא limits this to the מצורע. A rich מטמא מקדש who brought a poor offering has fulfilled his duty.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: "And if he is poor and cannot afford." Only for a מצורע does a rich person who brought a poor offering not fulfill his duty. But a rich person who made the מקדש impure and brought a poor offering has fulfilled his duty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word ״הוא״ (he) in the פסוק shows the rule is only for the מצורע. Other cases, like מטמא מקדש, follow רבי חגא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״הוא″ points to this person only, so the rule cannot be copied to other offerings. That saves רבי חגא. In other sliding-scale offerings, a rich person who brings a poor offering has fulfilled his duty.

keyTerms.meaning: Poor
He cannot afford it
One who entered the מקדש (or ate קדשים) while impure, and brings a sliding-scale offering

steps.whatToRemember: Only a rich מצורע fails with a poor person's offering, because of ״זאת״ and ״הוא״. A poor מצורע with a rich offering is fine (״תורת״). In other sliding-scale offerings like מטמא מקדש, a rich person who brings a poor offering has fulfilled his duty, as רבי חגא said.

phrases.english: The פסוק says:
"And if he is poor and cannot afford."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:21. The key word is הוּא, "he": this person only.

phrases.english: It is a מצורע where a rich person

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהֵבִיא קׇרְבַּן עָנִי הוּא דְּלֹא יָצָא,
phrases.english: who brought a poor person's offering does not fulfill his duty,
but a rich person who made the מקדש impure
who brought a poor person's offering has fulfilled his duty.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר קְרָא: ״וְאִם דַּל הוּא וְאֵין יָדוֹ מַשֶּׂגֶת״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 27 and closes the defense of רבי חגא
steps.terutzResolutionType: A limiting word (הוא) blocks spreading the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מצורע rule applies to all sliding-scale offerings
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule is unique to the מצורע; a rich מטמא מקדש with a poor offering fulfills his duty

steps.title: Lambs and goats are equal
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון teaches that lambs are listed before goats, but this does not mean lambs are better. A פסוק puts the lamb second, showing they are equal.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבי שמעון says: Lambs come before goats everywhere. One might think it is because they are better. So the פסוק says: "And if he brings a lamb as his offering for a חטאת". This teaches that both are equal.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. רבי שמעון explains that the order in which the תורה lists animals does not show which is better.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually lambs come first, which might suggest they are better. But in the חטאת of an individual, the goat comes first and the lamb comes after. Since the order flips, the two must be equal.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Lambs (sheep)
Goats
Better, choicer
Equal, of the same value

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Rabbi Shimon says:

phrases.aramaic: כְּבָשִׂים קוֹדְמִין אֶת הָעִזִּים בְּכׇל מָקוֹם,
phrases.english: Lambs come before goats everywhere,
one might think it is because they are better than them?
Therefore the פסוק says:
"And if he brings a lamb as his offering for a sin offering"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:32. Here the lamb comes after the goat, which the תורה mentioned first.

phrases.english: this teaches that both of them are equal.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: כְּבָשִׂים קוֹדְמִין אֶת הָעִזִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה, unrelated to the previous discussion
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lambs and goats are of equal value; the order in the תורה does not rank them

steps.title: תורין and בני יונה are equal
steps.stepSummary: תורין are listed before בני יונה, but a פסוק reverses the order, showing they are equal.
steps.simpleTranslation: תורין come before בני יונה everywhere. One might think it is because they are better. So the פסוק says: "And a בן יונה or a תור for a חטאת". This teaches that both are equal.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה makes the same point about birds. The usual order (תורין first) does not mean תורין are better.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like the lamb and goat, one פסוק flips the usual order and puts the בן יונה first. That shows neither bird is better than the other.

keyTerms.meaning: Turtledoves
Young pigeons

steps.whatToRemember: The order in which the תורה lists animals does not show which is better. Lambs and goats are equal, and תורין and בני יונה are equal, because in each pair a פסוק somewhere reverses the order.

phrases.aramaic: תּוֹרִין קוֹדְמִין לִבְנֵי יוֹנָה בְּכׇל מָקוֹם,
phrases.english: Turtledoves come before young pigeons everywhere,
one might think it is because they are better than them?
Therefore the פסוק says:
"And a young pigeon or a turtledove for a sin offering"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 12:6. Some versions leave out the words in round brackets; the word in square brackets matches the פסוק.

phrases.english: this teaches that both of them are equal.

steps.triggerLanguage: תּוֹרִין קוֹדְמִין לִבְנֵי יוֹנָה בְּכׇל מָקוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same reasoning from lambs and goats to birds
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תורין and בני יונה are of equal value; the order in the תורה does not rank them

steps.title: Father and mother are equal in the פסוקים
steps.stepSummary: The תורה usually names the father before the mother. One פסוק reverses the order, which shows that both are equal.
steps.simpleTranslation: The father is named before the mother everywhere. You might think this is because honoring the father comes before honoring the mother. So the פסוק says: 'Every man shall fear his mother and his father.' This teaches that both are equal.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה uses the same pattern it used for lambs and goats and for תורין and בני יונה. Here it applies the pattern to father and mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual order (father first) could make us think the father is more important. The פסוק in ויקרא puts the mother first. Because the תורה switches the order, we learn that neither one is ranked above the other.

keyTerms.meaning: Honoring, showing respect
'One might think': it sets up a wrong idea that the פסוק will correct
'The verse teaches': it brings the פסוק that corrects the wrong idea
Equal, of the same weight

phrases.english: The father is named before the mother everywhere [in the Torah],
One might think it is because honoring the father
comes before honoring the mother?
So the verse teaches:
'Every man shall fear his mother and his father,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:3

phrases.english: which teaches that both of them are equal.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל מִפְּנֵי שֶׁכִּיבּוּד הָאָב קוֹדֵם עַל כִּיבּוּד הָאֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the third example of the same pattern from steps 29 and 30: a reversed order in the פסוקים shows that the two items are equal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the פסוקים, the honor of father and mother is equal.

steps.title: In practice, the father's honor comes first
steps.stepSummary: חכמים rule that in practice the father comes first, because the mother is also obligated to honor the father.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the חכמים said: the father comes before the mother in every case, because the son and his mother are both obligated to honor his father.
steps.whatsHappening: Right after saying father and mother are equal, the משנה adds a practical rule. When the son cannot honor both at once, the father goes first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The equality from the פסוק is not cancelled. Both parents deserve the same honor. The father goes first only because the mother herself owes him honor, so serving the father first does not take away from her.

keyTerms.meaning: Comes first, takes precedence
Are obligated

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this step takes back 'both are equal.' The parents are equal in how much honor they deserve. Only the order, when the son cannot do both at once, goes to the father, for the reason given.

phrases.english: But the Sages said:
the father comes before the mother in every case,
because he and his mother
are both obligated to honor his father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a practical rule of order on top of the equality learned in step 31.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When both parents need something at once, the father is served first, because the mother also owes him honor.

steps.title: A son's main teacher comes before his father
steps.stepSummary: Using the same reasoning, the משנה rules that a son's main רב comes before his father, because the father must also honor the רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The same is true in Torah study. If the son merited to learn before a teacher, the teacher comes before the father in every case, because the son and his father are both obligated to honor his teacher.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה uses the reasoning from the father and mother case for another pair: the teacher and the father. This ends the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is the same as before. Whoever is owed honor by the other person comes first. Everyone must honor a Torah scholar, including the father, so the son's רב goes before the father.

keyTerms.meaning: Torah study
Merited, was privileged
His teacher, his main רב

steps.whatToRemember: One rule ties the end of the משנה together. When two people are owed honor, the one whom the other must also honor comes first: the father before the mother, and the רב before the father.

phrases.english: And the same is true in Torah study:
if the son merited [to learn] before the teacher,
phrases.notes: He means the teacher the son learned most of his Torah from.

phrases.aramaic: הָרַב קוֹדֵם אֶת הָאָב בְּכׇל מָקוֹם:
phrases.english: the teacher comes before the father in every case,
because he and his father
are both obligated to honor his teacher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the reasoning of step 32 to a new pair, the teacher and the father.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A son's main teacher comes before his father, because the father is also obligated to honor the teacher.

steps.title: The first of the courtyard's four cries
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא about four cries that came from the Temple courtyard. The first cry demanded that the sons of עלי be sent out.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: the Temple courtyard cried out four cries. The first cry was: 'Take out from here the sons of עלי, חפני and פנחס, who made the Sanctuary impure.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with a story-style ברייתא. It describes four cries, and here it gives the first one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The courtyard is described as if it could speak. The first cry asks for the removal of עלי's sons, חפני and פנחס, the כהנים who brought impurity into the היכל. This ברייתא continues past this step, so we are only at its start.

keyTerms.meaning: Cries, shouts
The Temple courtyard
The Sanctuary
Made impure

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
The Temple courtyard cried out four cries.
The first cry was:
'Take out from here the sons of Eli,
Chofni and Pinchas, who made the Sanctuary impure.'
phrases.notes: Their story is in שמואל א, chapters 2 and 4.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אַרְבַּע צְווֹחוֹת צָוְוחָה עֲזָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This starts the גמרא with a new ברייתא, after the משנה ended in step 33.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first of the four cries demanded the removal of חפני and פנחס for making the היכל impure.

steps.title: The second cry, about יוחנן בן נדבאי
steps.stepSummary: The second cry calls to open the gates for יוחנן בן נדבאי to eat קדשים. The ברייתא then begins to describe how much he ate.
steps.simpleTranslation: The second cry was: 'Open the gates, and let יוחנן בן נדבאי, the student of פינקאי, come in and fill his belly with holy offerings.' They said about בן נדבאי that he would eat forty סאה of young birds...
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves to the second cry. This time the courtyard calls for a person to be let in, and it starts to describe his huge appetite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first cry was against the sons of עלי. This cry welcomes יוחנן בן נדבאי to eat קדשים. The ברייתא then begins telling how much he ate, and the sentence continues past this step.

keyTerms.meaning: His belly
Holy offerings, consecrated to Heaven
A large unit of volume
Young birds, fledglings

phrases.english: The second cry was:
'Open the gates,
and let Yochanan ben Nedavai come in,
the student of Pinkai,
and fill his belly with holy offerings.'
They said about ben Nedavai
that he would eat forty se'ah of young birds

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of four cries from step 34 with the second one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The second cry welcomed יוחנן בן נדבאי to eat קדשים, and the ברייתא begins describing how much he ate.
